audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows disagreed across layers: phases[0..3].side read "Skill" while win[0..3] read "Azir", and phases[4].side read "Skill" while win[4] read "Twisted Fate" — with phases[4].why describing Azir winning every 2v2 at the exact stage the other layer gives to TF.
audit.why: The packet levelChart (Azir, Azir, Azir, Azir, Twisted Fate, Azir, Azir) matches the content layer row for row, and the whys support it: Azir out-ranges Wild Cards early, and Destiny (170/140/110s) is the one stage TF takes.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side set to Azir, phases[4].side set to Twisted Fate with its why rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text named "Shard of True Ice" as Azir's likely first completed item.
audit.why: That is a support item and it contradicts report[8] on the same page, which correctly prescribes a Nashor's Tooth rush. Naming the wrong first item breaks the whole first-item row of the chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] called the stun card "Gold Card (blue stun card)". Pick a Card's gold card is the stun; the blue card restores mana. The page also never mentioned that Pick a Card is an auto-attack reset, and breakdown.cooldowns held no digit.
audit.why: Kit flags Pick a Card as hardCC plus autoReset on a flat 6s, 200 range. missingInteractions flags autoreset-burst-tell: the wind-up, not the cast, is the cue to step back. Wild Cards is a 10000-range line projectile on 6/5.75/5.5/5.25/5s, so standing directly behind your own soldiers lines you up for all three cards.
audit.corrected: Card colour corrected, the auto-reset tell added to dosFull[0].d, real cooldowns added to breakdown.cooldowns, and the Wild Cards line interaction added to dontsFull[0].d.

audit.why: Destiny also reveals stealthed champions and gates him in over 1.5 seconds — the 1.5s channel is the window to reposition, which the page's advice to ping the cast already supports.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: The titles are about punishing his cooldown gap and about R discipline; both bodies explained trading instead.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to their titles with real numbers.

edits.before: Emperor's Divide online — the dive insurance and the insec flip. With R up you win every 2v2 your jungler joins.
edits.after: Destiny is 170s at rank 1: it reveals the map and gates him in, and that is his one window even while you own the wave.

edits.before: Twisted Fate wins by landing Pick a Card (Gold), denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Twisted Fate wins by gating in on Destiny, opening with the gold-card stun, and cashing the pick before your E is back.

edits.before: - Twisted Fate Pick a Card (Gold): matchup-defining — The locked gold card starts every trade and gank — back off the moment it glows yellow. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E Shifting Sands for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Pick a Card: a flat 6s — the locked gold card starts every trade and gank, so back off the moment it glows yellow and step up in the gap after. - Wild Cards is 6s falling to 5s. - Destiny is 170s at rank 1 and 110s maxed; ping every cast.

edits.before: The locked gold card starts every trade and gank — back off the moment it glows yellow. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: The gold card is an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up is the tell, not the cast. Step out as he loads it; Pick a Card is 6 seconds.

edits.before: W behind the wave, Q-drag the soldier through Twisted Fate on his last-hit, auto once through the soldier, step back — two-second trades he cannot answer without overextending.
edits.after: Stacked Deck is free and always ticking, but Pick a Card is his only lockdown — the 6 seconds after he spends a gold card is when you W-Q the full volley through him.

edits.before: That is Twisted Fate’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Wild Cards run a line and pierce — never stand directly behind your sand.

edits.before: Standing at max soldier range admiring your poke with E on cooldown — that is the engage window every Twisted Fate player is waiting for.
edits.after: Emperor's Divide is 120s at rank 1 — spend it to shove a card-gank off you, never on poke, or the Destiny collapse arrives with no answer.

edits.before: Carry through siege control — soldiers take plates, R denies engages, and your DPS curve outlasts every assassin spike in the lobby.
edits.after: Carry through range — soldiers hold the plates while he needs 200 range to land a card, and Emperor's Divide throws the Destiny collapse back out.

edits.before: Azir's ranged soldier zoning outclasses TF's early Wild Card poke before he has Pick a Card up reliably.
edits.after: Azir's ranged soldier zoning outclasses TF's early Wild Cards poke before he has Pick a Card up reliably.

edits.before: Your first completed item (usually Liandry's or Shard of True Ice) spikes your wave clear and poke damage hard, letting you push and roam off level-6 pressure before he can capitalize.
edits.after: Your first completed item, Nashor's Tooth, spikes your soldier DPS and wave clear hard, letting you crash and roam off the level-6 window before he can capitalize on Destiny.

edits.before: Hold E (Shifting Sands) to dash away or interrupt if he all-ins with Gold Card
edits.after: Hold E (Shifting Sands) to dash clear the instant he loads a gold-card wind-up

edits.before: Land Gold Card (blue stun card) to lock you down before you can wall off
edits.after: Land the gold card off Pick a Card to stun you before you can wall off

notes: The packet flags that the level chart contradicts the data (Azir wins only 43.37% over 814 games while the chart gives him 6 of 7 stages). I did not rebalance the rows: nothing in either kit tells me which stage is actually wrong, and the chart is at least internally coherent, so per the chart rule I left the verdicts alone and only removed the cross-layer disagreements. This is worth a human decision — the chart reads far friendlier than a 43% win rate. Also, suspectNames flags "Gold Card" in spikes[1].text as a probable wrong name; it is a false positive — the gold card is the stun card produced by Pick a Card, and it is the correct term. The genuine error in that area was the reverse one, in wants.foe[0], which called the stun card blue; that is fixed above.
